page: Amazon Web Services i4i.metal is a bare-metal storage-optimized server built for high-throughput I/O and data-intensive compute environments. The system is powered by an x86_64 dual-socket class Intel Xeon 8375C processor providing 64 physical cores, 128 dedicated vCPUs operating at 3.5 GHz, and a 54 MB L3 cache. It incorporates 1024 GB of DDR4 system memory running at 3 GHz (yielding 8 GB per vCPU) and bundles 30,000 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Network connectivity is delivered via a baseline bandwidth of 75 Gbps, while GPU hardware acceleration is not present on this host.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate superior multi-threaded and I/O capability alongside moderate single-thread ratings. Multi-core performance is confirmed by a PassMark CPU score of 87,524.92 and stress-ng multi-core metric of 125,019.7, both placing in the top tiers, whereas single-core metrics register in the middle 50% percentile across Geekbench and stress-ng tests. Large-block memory bandwidth tests show read throughput at 338.82 GB/sec and write throughput at 132.78 GB/sec. Application benchmarks reflect high transaction capacity, capturing 109.81 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations and 72.29 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

The bare-metal hardware profile yields high resource density and low virtualization overhead, offering qualitative cost efficiency for scale-up deployments requiring immense integrated NVMe storage alongside large memory allocations. The primary architectural tradeoff is the absence of discrete GPU accelerators and moderate single-core speeds compared to specialized burst or compute-centric chipsets. Amazon Web Services i4i.metal is best suited for high-transaction relational and NoSQL databases, distributed real-time search clusters, in-memory caches, and heavy software compilation pipelines.
